edges.description: Hyperactive LRRK2 hyperphosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases on a conserved switch-II residue.
Dysregulated Rab-dependent trafficking impairs the autophagy-lysosomal pathway.
Impaired autophagy-lysosomal clearance permits alpha-synuclein accumulation and Lewy body formation.
Alpha-synuclein pathology and the upstream cellular dysfunction drive loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons.
Loss of nigral dopaminergic projections depletes striatal dopamine and unbalances the basal ganglia motor circuit.

edges.description: Resting tremor is a cardinal component of the parkinsonian syndrome.
Bradykinesia is a cardinal component of the parkinsonian syndrome.
Rigidity is a cardinal component of the parkinsonian syndrome.
Postural instability emerges as the parkinsonian syndrome progresses.

nodes.description: Accumulation and aggregation of alpha-synuclein into Lewy bodies is the common (though pleomorphic in LRRK2 disease) downstream pathology, shared with idiopathic Parkinson disease.

LRRK2 regulates macroautophagy, chaperone-mediated autophagy, and lysosomal activity; pathogenic LRRK2 perturbs this pathway, and declining lysosomal activity potentiates accumulation of alpha-synuclein.

nodes.description: Heterozygous pathogenic LRRK2 variants augment the intrinsic serine/threonine kinase activity of the protein; the most common variant, G2019S, activates the kinase two- to threefold. This is the initiating molecular lesion.
Because pathogenic variants act by augmenting kinase activity, LRRK2 kinase inhibitors are in clinical development as a targeted, potentially disease-modifying approach; not yet established.

evidence.reference_title: Phosphoproteomics reveals that Parkinson's disease kinase LRRK2 regulates a subset of Rab GTPases.
evidence.snippet: This has motivated the development of LRRK2 kinase inhibitors

nodes.description: Symptomatic dopaminergic replacement, most commonly levodopa combined with carbidopa, is the mainstay and is generally effective, as in idiopathic Parkinson disease.

evidence.snippet: Symptomatic treatment of the motor features of parkinsonism is the same as for other known causes of Parkinson disease: pharmacologic replacement of dopamine, most commonly accomplished with the precursor of dopamine, levodopa, combined with carbidopa.

nodes.description: Progressive degeneration of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons and their striatal projections, the lesion that produces the motor syndrome.
Typical parkinsonism, largely indistinguishable from idiopathic Parkinson disease.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features of LRRK2-associated Parkinson's disease in central Norway.
evidence.snippet: The clinical features included asymmetric resting tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity with a good response to levodopa and could not be distinguished from idiopathic Parkinson's disease.
Dystonia and gait abnormalities that may include freezing and postural instability may also be present.

nodes.description: Pathogenic-LRRK2-driven phosphorylation of Rab GTPases reduces their affinity for regulatory proteins including Rab GDP dissociation inhibitors, dysregulating the Rab-controlled membrane-trafficking machinery.
